page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by four NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs totaling 64 GB of VRAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-core ratio, and connects to cloud infrastructure through a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data operations.

Benchmark evaluations reveal an architecture tailored for multi-threaded and GPU-offloaded computing rather than raw single-core speed. The Intel Xeon 8163 processor demonstrates modest single-threaded throughput, recording a weak stress-ng single-core score of 1103.89 and a bottom-tier gzip compression rate of 19.1 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics remain solid, with stress-ng multi-core testing reaching 23575.63 and PassMark CPU reaching 21092.78. Memory bandwidth shows balanced performance across uncached reads (118.4 GB/sec) and writes (57.05 GB/sec), supporting high-throughput in-memory operations like Redis SET workloads at 22.1 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, this instance trades bleeding-edge CPU instruction extensions and local storage for substantial parallel graphics processing capacity. With four discrete Volta-generation GPUs providing massive matrix and parallel computing capabilities alongside 128 GB of host memory, the hardware density favors specialized computational workloads. It is functionally suited for deep learning training, AI model inferencing, distributed GPU-accelerated computing pipelines, scientific simulations, and parallel video rendering tasks.
